PASS WITH NOTES — performance/277, exact head5e700abc3e61c0ff273cc7531c5b6c77bc193a3c, static pre-deployment review under C33/C34. No demonstrated normal-use performance blocker. No builds, tests, reloads or restarts run. The two premise corrections below are material accounting notes, not hidden launch costs.

## Loops, deadlines and per-seat scaling

1. Native inbox claim wait (delivery/mod.rs:1967-1988,2255-2273). The idle deadline is55s and is checked only after no claim was handed off; no in-flight claim is cut. IMPORTANT: this head does NOT implement it only through the existing delivery tick. It explicitly adds tokio::time::sleep_until(idle_until) at2270 in each pending native claim's select. That is one additional in-process Tokio deadline future per pending request, recreated when another select arm wins, not an OS process, independent task or new periodic poll. Existing idle500ms checks (up to2wakes/s per waiting seat) and during-turn15s backstop remain. With42one-pending-claim clients: at most42additional resident deadline futures, alongside up to84existing idle checks/s; at82:82and164/s. The55s deadline may wake between an existing500ms/15s wake; do not claim zero new timer registrations or that the idle answer rides only the global delivery tick.

2. Native receiver reconciliation (delivery:767-812; lib.rs:763-794). Same existing delivery TickLoop, configured delivery_interval_secs (default5s), also woken by earliest lease deadline. D1 adds an in-memory lapse-set prune and membership check; no new reconciliation loop/timer. The new retain scans the live-seat vector for each saved lapsed id: O(L*N), L<=N; upper1764comparisons/pass at42,6724at82, in addition to prior lease-map pruning. It does not read or append the spine on every healthy tick. The set holds only live native seats after reconciliation.

3. Existing native heartbeat loop. Lease renewal remains at lease/3 (normally60s lease→20s, aboutN/20heartbeats/s:2.1at42), with its existing retry backoff. D1 adds an in-memory remove; only a told lapsed→renewed edge publishes. One event/log for the first lapse and one for its renewal, per lapse cycle, not per tick/heartbeat. Existing global native lock is held through restore and edge publication: startup/write latency can delay other native operations, so measure it after bounce. No new heartbeat cadence or auth restart trigger.

4. D2 registration refusals (registration.rs:343-405; refusals.rs:39-69). Triggered by actual refused service attempts; no timer/sweeper. Real-seat eligibility uses existing attempt counters, not a new registry lookup. Suppressed repeats do no new store read/write. Cost is NOT merely an O(1) lookup: admit takes a mutex, scans at most512entries to expire them, allocates a seat String even on a suppressed duplicate, and scans/clones the oldest entry on full-window insertion. Bounded and cold enough for the expected refusal cadence; no code-change request under C34. An admitted pair appends one event/log. With42seats each repeating one code and no eviction, at most42initial records then42/600=0.07records/s averaged over later windows.512is a memory bound, NOT a global write-rate cap: live-pair eviction permits a pair to be told sooner, and churn over512pairs can record every eligible refusal. refusals_evicted exposes that pressure. Observe it after deploy rather than promising a hard512events/10min ceiling.

5. PA digest: same60s/default watchdog path and existing in-memory lapse read; only advice text changes. No restart is automatically added by that text. F212 trigger/rate unchanged. Copilot store.mjs production delta is comment-only.

## Launch-site check

Exact worktree HEAD verified. Diff against the main merge base changes16files and has no spawn_sites.rs delta. Traced added delivery/registration/refusal paths: no Command/spawn/exec, spawn_blocking or new worker/task launch. EventBus append and eprintln run in process. Therefore zero ADDED process-launch sites/per-tick-per-seat launches; pre-existing registration/command-recovery launch costs are not claimed to be zero. There IS the per-request deadline future noted above.

## Boot restore bound and today's spine

restore_receiver_edges (delivery:507-550) is OnceCell get_or_init, called before the first renewing heartbeat or reconciliation under native_lock. Once per daemon: one filtered live-Copilot roster read, then one latest_matching call per live native Copilot seat. Production SqliteSpine::latest_matching (spine.rs:367-394) opens one read snapshot PER SEAT and executes one LATEST_MATCHING_SQL per kind. There are TWO kinds, so2Nindexed LIMIT1SELECTs, plus one per-seat schema check and BEGIN/ROLLBACK, and the roster/schema read. It is not one bulk query, nor one SQL SELECT per seat. At42:84edgeSELECTs; at today's82daemon-wide native seats:164. It restores at mostN ids and is O(N*log(spine_rows)) index work rather than a full-history fold. No cadence repeats that read after OnceCell completes, including its handled-error path.

Read-only diagnostic at2026-11-20T02:18:33Z on ~/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite: schema47,3100seat rows,1,080,705spine rows (max seq4,671,009),82live native Copilot rows across the daemon, not asserted to be42in this project's cohort. EXPLAIN for exact production SQL: SEARCH spine_events USING INDEX spine_by_seat_kind (seat=? AND kind=?), no full-seat history scan/sort. Both new edge kinds are absent for those seats. In one fixed read-only snapshot,164exact production SELECTs all missed in0.314666ms wall/0.315ms Python CPU, after metadata probes warmed them. Thus no event payload row was read. This is a warm SQLite probe-cost measurement, NOT full Rust/SQLx restore latency: excludes pooled async dispatch, per-seat schema/transaction work, roster descriptor decode, contention and cold I/O. The diagnostic COUNT(*) itself took2.543s; boot restore DOES NOT run that count. No credentials, transport inbox or message payloads inspected. Receipt /tmp/performance-277-spine-cost.json, embedded below. A hard wall-time guarantee under database contention is not established by this measurement.

## Is the extra idle HTTP traffic acceptable against F222's ~16%?

Yes, as a STATIC capacity judgement, not a measured post-deploy CPU claim. For42continuously idle seats, excluding retry pauses:42/65=0.64615→42/55=0.76364claims/s, +0.11748/s (1.1818x). The unchanged empty-page/timeout paths both double250ms pause to5s: at capped steady idle42/70=0.6→42/60=0.7/s, +0.1/s (1.1667x). Active messages, holds, retries and during-turn waits change observed rates. For82daemon-wide idle seats the corresponding capped estimate is1.17143→1.36667/s (+0.19524/s). These are modeled cohort rates, not measured current arrivals.

This keeps HTTP completion rate below~0.8/s for the stated42-seat idle cohort, adds no launches, and does not increase the existing2Hz per-idle-claim polling frequency. The F22215.970% live baseline was a different workload/daemon; request rate cannot be converted into a claimed CPU saving or percentage overhead. The one-shot indexed restore and edge-triggered writes are acceptable at measured scale with the bounds/eviction caveat above.

## Owed after merge/bounce (parent-controlled)

Take four ping+CPU-TIME+RSS readings over~4min on one PID/commit, splitting any interval across a restart. Report GET /v1/inbox OK/refused deltas/rates and total traffic, native cohort size/adoption, heartbeat/register routes, registrations.by_outcome and refusals_evicted; compare like workloads rather than asserting F222's16% is a current control. Read data.spawns twice at known interval (all by_op deltas), plus just spawn-rate --seconds20 for whole-machine receipts. Watch first-heartbeat/restore delay, lease lapsed/renewed edge frequency and refusal event growth, especially across a second bounce. Empty-page success should clear a real stale banner, not client timeouts; ownership of that behavioral smoke remains with coder/reviewer. No live277before/after or55s-handler runtime proof is claimed here; source, existing fixtures and isolated read-only SQL probes are the evidence for this static verdict.
